chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): 'How is it befitting for us that we conduct ourselves regarding what is between us and our people, and between those who intermingle with us from the people, from those who are not upon our matter (al-Wilayah)?'

He said: 'Look to your Imams, those whom you follow and emulate, and do as they do. By Allah! Indeed they visit their sick ones, attend their funerals, give testimony for them and against them, and return the trusts to them.'

key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: Our matter/cause — a technical term for al-Wilayah, commitment to the Imamate
key_terms.الْأَمَانَة: Trust/entrustment — goods, money, or responsibilities held in trust for another person
key_terms.خُلَطَاء: Those who intermingle/mix — referring to non-Shia neighbors, business partners, and social contacts

ai.seo_question: How should Shia Muslims interact with non-Shia people according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked by his companion Mu'awiya ibn Wahb how Shia Muslims should interact with non-Shia neighbors and associates. The Imam directed them to observe the conduct of the Imams themselves, who exemplify universal civic virtues: visiting the sick, attending funerals regardless of religious affiliation, giving just testimony even when unfavorable, and faithfully returning entrusted property. This teaching reflects the Imam's guidance during the Abbasid period, when Shia communities lived as minorities among broader Muslim society and needed practical guidance on maintaining their identity while engaging honorably with all people.
word_analysis: those who intermingle with us/our associates

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How is it befitting for us that we behave regarding what is between us and our people, and between those who intermingle with us from the people, from the ones who are not upon our matter (Al-Wilayah)?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be looking at your Imams<sup>asws</sup>, those whom you are being Guided with, so you should be doing what they<sup>asws</sup> are doing. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! They<sup>asws</sup> are consoling their sick ones, and they<sup>asws</sup> are attending their funerals, and they<sup>asws</sup> are establishing the testimonies for them and against them, and they<sup>asws</sup> are paying back the entrustments to them’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “Once I asked the Imam (a.s.) ‘What is the proper way to deal with ourselves and our people, our associates of the people who do not believe as we do?’

The Imam said, ‘Look to your ‘A’immah (plural of Imam) whom you follow and do what they do. By Allah, they, (‘A’immah) visit their sick people, attend their funerals, present their testimony for and against them and return their trust.’”
